subject: Packaging safety net, downgrade pathways, and surge credit options
messages:
From: Anna Li <anna@clearwell.com>
To: Jonas Weber <jonas@redwood.com>
Cc: Ryan Cho <ryan.cho@clearwell.com>
Date: 2027-06-18T09:12:00-07:00
Subject: Clarify packaging: downgrade pathways and temporary seat pooling

Jonas —

Thanks for the demo last week. We’re close to an internal decision but procurement has two asks I need your help clarifying before we present to the execs:

1) Downgrade risk: if Clearwell needs to step down capacity mid-year (seasonal demand swings), what options preserve the advanced features we use for clinical workflows (function calling, streaming, and the custom reranker)? Are there guaranteed rollback windows or prorated credits?

2) Surge credits & temporary seat pooling: we have predictable spikes around audit windows — can we get burst credits or temporary seat pooling that won’t count against committed throughput, and what’s the provisioning lead time?

3) Pricing anchor: procurement will push for a higher discount if we commit to a 12–18 month agreement. What’s the ceiling on discounting for their tier, and are there feature carveouts we can use to keep unit economics intact?

I’m attaching our Multipath MAP for context (clearwell_multipath_MAP_v1.docx). Happy to hop on a quick call this afternoon if useful.

—Anna
Anna Li
Head of Product Operations
Clearwell Therapeutics

From: Jonas Weber <jonas@redwood.com>
To: Anna Li <anna@clearwell.com>
Cc: Ryan Cho <ryan.cho@clearwell.com>, Ben Carter <ben@redwood.com>, Lauren Bishop <lauren@redwood.com>
Date: 2027-06-18T11:03:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Clarify packaging: downgrade pathways and temporary seat pooling

Anna — thanks for the clear list. High level answers below; I’ll formalize with a short proposal this afternoon and include a pricing grid.

- Downgrade / rollback: We can offer a 60-day swapback window after any stepdown where shipped features (reranker, streaming, function calls) remain available for 30–90 days (configurable by feature) while you migrate. Proration: we provide token-credit prorates for committed throughput reductions on a monthly basis.

- Surge credits / temporary pooling: We can provide a one-time pool of surge tokens (example: 200k tokens over 2 months) or enable temporary seat pooling for up to 45 days with 48‑hour provisioning notice. Pool size and lead time can be tuned based on committed spend.

- Discounting: Standard flexibility: up to 10% for 12 months at the tier you’re evaluating; with a 12–18 month commit and a modest usage guarantee we can stretch to 12–15% with conditional carveouts (e.g., exclude advanced retraining seats or limit custom quantization runs).

Recommended quick package to present to procurement:
- Compact+FeaturePack: compact tier (preserves low-latency routing) + bundled reranker feature pack (kept for 90 days post-stepdown)
- Terms: 12% first-year discount, 60-day swapback, 200k surge token credit (2 months), prorated credits on downgrade monthly

I’ll loop Ben and Lauren for approval on the discount and surge-credit sizing and share a redlined term sheet you can circulate. If procurement wants a deeper SLA exception we’ll escalate to legal.

Best,
Jonas
Jonas Weber
Account Executive, Redwood Inference

Attachment: redwood_pricing_grid_v2.xlsx
From: Jonas Weber <jonas@redwood.com>
To: Ben Carter <ben@redwood.com>, Lauren Bishop <lauren@redwood.com>
Date: 2027-06-18T15:20:00-07:00
Subject: FW: Clearwell packaging asks — proposed concessions

Ben / Lauren — forwarding Anna’s asks. Quick internal proposal so we can come back with concrete numbers:

Context: Clearwell is a mid-market clinical SaaS with sensitive workloads (PHI-adjacent). They want a safe downgrade path + surge credits and will lean on procurement for discounting.

Proposal (internal):
- Discount: offer 12% Year 1 (flat) if they commit 12 months and agree to a minimum monthly throughput threshold (we should propose a midpoint guarantee).
- Surge: grant 200k token surge credit usable over any two consecutive months within the first 12 months.
- Swapback / Downgrade: 60-day swapback window. Preserve elite features for 90 days after stepdown for a smooth migration; after 90 days, features will be gated behind a restoration fee or re-up.
- Proration: prorated token-credit refund for committed throughput reductions on a monthly basis (no retroactive credits beyond 30 days).
- Escalation: legal to review SLA carveouts — if procurement asks for longer preservation we’ll require a premium (additional 3–4% concession).

Risks: margin erosion if they step down soon after a heavy onboarding period. Suggest we tie the full 12% discount to a minimum spend guarantee (HubSpot deal notes: CW-9243).

If you’re good with that, I’ll send the formal proposal to Anna with the DocuSign link and redlined T&Cs.

—Jonas

From: Jonas Weber <jonas@redwood.com>
To: Anna Li <anna@clearwell.com>
Cc: Ryan Cho <ryan.cho@clearwell.com>, Ben Carter <ben@redwood.com>, Lauren Bishop <lauren@redwood.com>
Date: 2027-06-19T14:05:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Clarify packaging: downgrade pathways and temporary seat pooling

Anna — thanks for the quick turnaround. Per internal alignment we can commit to the following package if Clearwell signs a 12-month commitment by next Friday:

Offer summary (final):
- Pricing: 12% discount Year 1 applied to committed throughput spend.
- Surge: 200,000 token surge credit usable in any two consecutive months during the first 12 months.
- Downgrade / Swapback: 60-day swapback window. During the first 90 days after a stepdown we’ll preserve your reranker, streaming, and function-calling access so you have time to migrate. After 90 days the preserved features will be gated and require a restoration fee to re-enable.
- Proration: Monthly prorated token-credit adjustment for any committed throughput reductions (applied to the next billing cycle). No retroactive credits beyond the 30-day lookback.
- Conditions: the 12% discount is contingent on a minimum monthly throughput guarantee (I’ve listed a reasonable floor in the attached pricing grid). If procurement asks for a longer feature preservation window we can offer that for an additional 3% concession.

Next steps:
1) I’ve attached the pricing grid for the package (redwood_pricing_grid_v2.xlsx) and prepared a DocuSign with the outlined terms: https://www.docusign.com/sign/CW-9243-Redwood.
2) If this matches what procurement needs, confirm by COB Friday and I’ll route to Legal for a quick SLAs carveout review.

Happy to discuss on a quick call if Anna or Ryan want to walk through the swapback mechanics.

Best,
Jonas Weber
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
